turns.question: Who sold the painting, and when did it surface?
turns.reply: The painting was first publicly recorded by the Van Doren Gallery in Amsterdam, which announced its acquisition in March 1952 as a previously unrecorded panel attributed to Cornelis van Leyden (The Widow’s Supper — sale record, 1952).  The gallery subsequently sold the work later that same year to a private collector in Rotterdam for a substantial, undisclosed sum (The Widow’s Supper — sale record, 1952).

turns.question: How did the painting reach the museum?
turns.reply: The painting entered the permanent collection of the Museum of Modern Art in 1941. It was acquired through the Lillie P. Bliss Bequest, according to the museum’s record. Thus the museum’s holdings of the work derive solely from that bequest. (Source: “The Starry Night (1889)”)
